title: OpenPlanning Application Schema v1
description: Defines an Application: the bridge between a Jurisdiction (who reviews) and a Parcel (what is reviewed). Two shapes are supported, dispatched on the presence of source.source_document_sha256: (1) Observation merge: each item lists `fields` (and optional `retract`) that ONE source document observed on ONE date; the loader merges field-by-field by observed_at into Application.field_provenance. Spec path is conventionally applications/by-source/<source_doc_sha256>.json so re-emit of the same source bytes is idempotent. (2) Full-row upsert (legacy hand-authored fixtures): items carry full row state; identity is optional id (uuid) or natural key (jurisdiction, application_number) > (jurisdiction, file_number) > (jurisdiction, title).

source.description: When source_document_sha256 is set, the loader uses observation-merge mode and `observed_at` is required.

observed_at.description: Source document's authored date. Drives merge precedence per field.

source_document_sha256.description: sha256 of the source document. Loader resolves to a Document row by (municipality, sha256). The Document fixture must load earlier in the manifest.

municipality.description: Municipality these applications belong to. Used to scope parcel and project lookups; the jurisdiction_abbreviation on each application is resolved within this municipality.

project_ref.description: Reference to a Project within the municipality. Resolved by id when present, otherwise by slug.

parcel_ref.description: See parcel/v1#/$defs/parcel_ref for the canonical definition. Structured natural-key reference: {street_number?, street_name, street_suffix?, city, state}.

citation.description: An embedded citation linking the host application to a legal.Block. The host's jurisdiction is inherited; the spec only carries section_number for block resolution. Re-loading the same fixture is idempotent (keyed on (jurisdiction, block, application)).

section_number.description: Block.section_number (e.g. '180-137'). Resolved within the host application's jurisdiction. If multiple versions exist, the current version (is_current=True) is preferred.

excerpt.description: Verbatim quote from the host document supporting the citation.

note.description: Editor's note explaining the citation's relevance.

created_by.description: Origin tag, e.g. 'openplanning' or 'seed'. Defaults to 'openplanning' when omitted.

document_ref.description: Reference to a documents.Document within the municipality. Resolved by source_url first, then by name.

process_assignment.description: Enrolls the application in a ReviewProcess (creates an ApplicationProcess row). Resolved by (application.jurisdiction, name). The model permits multiple processes per application (one per commission), so this is an array; the typical case is a single entry.

name.description: ReviewProcess name, unique within the application's jurisdiction.

current_node.description: Current node ID in the process graph. Empty string when not started or when the process is complete.

is_complete.description: True when the process has reached a terminal state.

entity_ref.description: Reference to a global Entity in the rolodex. The natural key is `name`, which is globally unique (case-insensitive). Either a bare string (the name) or an object `{name, id?}` is accepted ,  `id` is the canonical UUID when known. `entity_type` is not part of the ref because the type is often unknown at the time of reference (e.g. AI-extracted applicants where the source PDF doesn't disclose whether 'Joy Property' is a sole proprietorship or a corporation). The Entity record itself owns its type. The loader does not auto-create entities; missing entities are logged and the FK is left null.

oneOf.description: Bare entity name ,  the canonical natural key.

application.description: Application item. Two shapes: (1) Observation-merge item carries `fields` (and optional `retract`) which the loader merges into the row. Identified by (jurisdiction_abbreviation, file_number) with title fallback. (2) Legacy full-row item carries scalar fields directly at the top level (title, parcel, applicant, dates, etc.) for upsert.

id.description: Stable UUID primary key. When set, this is the canonical identifier across environments. Optional in the observation-merge shape.

jurisdiction_abbreviation.description: Reviewing jurisdiction, resolved within the municipality (e.g. 'PC').

fields.description: Observation-merge mode only: fields this source document actually observed. Missing keys are not deletions. Scalar values pass through; refs (parcel, applicant) resolve via existing helpers.

retract.description: Observation-merge mode only: fields to set to null with this spec's observed_at.

title.description: Human-readable application title. Used as a natural-key fallback when file_number is absent.

application_number.description: Public-facing application number. First-priority natural key within the jurisdiction.

file_number.description: Internal file number (e.g. 'P-23-0026'). Second-priority natural key within the jurisdiction.

parcel.description: Reviewed Parcel, resolved by street address within the municipality.

applicant.description: The Entity that applied. Hermetic ref carrying name + entity_type, resolved against the global rolodex by name (case-insensitive). Never auto-creates.

description.description: Free-form description. Plain text or markdown.

current_status.description: Free-form workflow status string (e.g. 'Approved', 'In Review', 'Referred to Town Council').

project.description: Optional Project to attach via the Project.applications M2M. Resolved within the municipality.

documents.description: Documents to attach via the Application.documents M2M. Each is resolved by source_url first, then name.

processes.description: ReviewProcess enrollments for this application. Each entry creates or updates an ApplicationProcess row keyed by (application, review_process).

citations.description: Code citations attached to this application. Each entry creates or updates a Citation row keyed by (jurisdiction, block, application). Edges are additive across loads.
